lots.guide_summary: Close entries run A$65 to A$906 (rate USD 1 = AUD 1.437). SOLD: Hobart A$65 to A$90 for one stepped opal shade or one complete stepped pendant; Leonard Joel A$250 for a two-shade chrome opal pendant; Nordic 1930s chrome three or four light opal fittings A$290 to A$537 each, with an outlier at A$887. UNSOLD: Leonard Joel three-light pink-shade chrome fitting passed at A$100 to 200 estimate. ASKING: restored dealer chandelier A$906 (eBay A$350 snippet is a lead only, not in the range). No twin (chrome fitting with stepped opal shades, in parts) found sold.
lots.working: No exact twin sold, so the lowest lot-scale close SOLD is used as a conservative floor: Leonard Joel IT122 lot 185, A$250 hammer (24 Mar 2026), one two-shade chrome opal Deco pendant. Lot 239 holds two fittings and about seven stepped shades, more than that lot, but needs assembly and rewiring, so A$250 for the pair is a fair floor. keep_max = 250 / 1.22 = 204.9, round down to $200 hammer ($244 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$300 hammer for the pair sold unwired in an Australian room (above the single Leonard Joel pendant, well under Nordic per-fitting prices of A$290 to A$537 because ours is unwired and in parts), less about 15% auction commission = A$255; 255 / 2.44 = 104.5, round down to $100 hammer. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup at Invermay). Rewiring by a licensed electrician is extra and not costed here; it would cut the flip margin.
lots.confidence_reason: No maker mark read, view partial (fittings unassembled, shade count and arm count uncertain), age unclear (very bright chrome could mean replating or a later copy), and no same-item SOLD: max bids rest on close-class sales, mostly Nordic.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gowans 367291 (plain large milk glass ceiling shade A$40, not Deco or stepped) and Gowans 370796 (qty of 1970s brass hanging fittings A$190, not Deco or chrome): not comparable. Kept the eBay A$350 search-page snippet as a lead only (not verified, no listing URL). Every other URL was opened and price, date and kind matched the researcher.
lots.key_photo_findings: Contact sheet: about seven white stepped opal shades (three or four tiers), a pear-shaped chrome hub with scroll ornaments and a spherical chrome hub, two chrome bell canopies, two ribbed chrome rods, turned chrome finials under each shade holder, old braided cloth flex plus cut modern wire with green earth, and a paper string tag. No visible chips on shades in these photos, no maker stamp visible.
lots.condition: Unassembled, unwired (cloth flex old, wires cut). Chrome bright with no obvious pitting in photos. Shades look whole but rims not visible close up. Needs assembly, rewiring and electrical testing before use.
lots.question_for_armitage: How many shades and arms are there in total, and do both fittings have all arms, holders and fixing screws? Any chips or cracks on the shade rims? Any maker mark on the canopies or shade holders? Is the chrome original or replated?

lots.guide_summary: All AUD, no conversion needed for the range. 21 close Gowans SOLD hammers from Oct 2025 to Oct 2026 run A$26 to A$450 (median about A$55); most ordinary boxes of stacks made A$40 to A$70, the one album lot A$55, and four bulk or older lots A$280 to A$450. No UNSOLD label lots found. The only ASKING entries are stale US dealer single-label lists (1999 and 2006), not in the range. No sold result found for Lalla, Dollar Bird, Blue Bird, Twin W or Buy Me labels.
lots.working: Lots clearly smaller than lot 291 are set aside. The smallest close SOLD of similar scale is Gowans 442056, about 13 designs in crisp stacks, A$95 hammer (9 Oct 2026); lot 291 has perhaps fewer stack designs but adds three albums and interstate and overseas labels. keep_max = 95 / 1.22 = 77.9, round down to $75 hammer ($91.50 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$120 hammer back through Gowans (above the A$95 comparable, well below the A$280 to A$450 bulk results), less about 15% vendor commission = A$102; 102 / 2.44 = 41.8, round down to $40 hammer. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup).
lots.confidence_reason: Labels are clearly read in the photos and many Gowans SOLD records were opened, but none is the same lot; the count of labels, the album contents and the backs are unknown, and the A$26 to A$450 spread is wide.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as not crate-label lots or not comparable: Gowans 382671 (glassware box with a few labels, A$2), 388872 (tin wrappers, A$2), 379502 (flags and mixed, A$10), 395849 and 421329 and 431023 and 438378 (mostly Browns pie apple tin strips, A$5 to A$30), 419129 (mostly fruit tin labels, A$50), 395343 (mostly can and jam wrappers, A$120), 439094 (labels with 25 rubber stamps, A$50). Dropped fruitcratelabels.com specials page (US$285 for 36 US Northwest pear labels, 1999): different labels and market. All Gowans records re-opened and matched the researcher on title and price. Stale dealer single-label lists re-filed as category guide, not in the guide range.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: about three spiral sleeve albums (Lalla gold cover, Dollar Bird cover, Southern Isle) and about eight loose stacks, several copies of each design. Photo 2: Lalla gold foil and white versions, W.A.G. Walker & Sons, Riverside, Tamar Valley, Distinguished Quality seal; blue Fancy Pears; magenta Tas Fruit. Photos 3 to 6: Dollar Bird Apples (Producers Co-operative Distributing Society, Sydney, Devonport agency listed), Blue Bird (Crown Fruit Co, Kelowna BC), Twin W (Wells & Wade, Wenatchee, 40 lbs net), Buy Me Canadian Apples. Labels look crisp, bright and unused; sleeves show reflections. Backs not shown.
lots.condition: Appears crisp and unused with bright colour; slight curl on loose stacks. Backs, glue residue and any foxing not visible. Count unknown (likely 100 to 300).
lots.question_for_armitage: Roughly how many labels are there, and how many different designs? Are the album sleeves full, and are there other overseas or mainland labels besides those photographed? Any staining, foxing or glue on the backs?

lots.question_for_armitage: Are all three joints and the bell free of cracks, and do the pads seal (has it been played or serviced recently)? Is there a serial number on the body? Any bent keys?
